chunks: From him, from Fadalah, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): A man had dirhams owed to a person, so he gifted them to him, then he revoked the gift, then he gifted them to him again, then he revoked again, then he gifted them to him, then he died. He (the Imam) said: 'They belong to the one to whom they were gifted.'

key_terms.لِلَّذِي وُهِبَ لَهُ: To the one to whom it was gifted

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on revoking a gift multiple times before death?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that repeated revocations do not invalidate the final act of gift-giving, emphasizing the donor's intent to make the transfer permanent upon death. This ruling highlights the distinction between temporary conditional gifts and irrevocable transfers in Shia jurisprudence, ensuring the creditor retains the wealth as a finalized gift rather than a revocable loan. The narration underscores the principle that the last declared state of the gift prevails in cases of multiple 'ruju' before the donor's demise.
